Place your Wireless Energy Monitor, give it LV power, and right-click it to open the GUI.

The redstone mode button cycles §efive modes§r: Off, High Level (signal when EU is above §eParam1§r), Low Level (below §eParam1§r), High-Hysteresis (output above §eParam1§r, cancel only below §eParam2§r) and Low-Hysteresis. Output is full strength §e15§r. The anchor toggle switches what is measured: wireless energy storage or EU/t status. Param values are typed in directly, scientific notation like §e1.5E6§r works.

Energy refreshes every §e5 seconds§r over a §e300 second window§r; redstone reacts every §e2 ticks§r. Wire the output into a comparator circuit and let the grid guard itself.
